The query joins each order line to its product and sums quantity_product * price in euro cents. Its filters include 2026-03-01 00:00:00 and exclude 2026-06-01 00:00:00, implementing the required half-open period; COALESCE ensures a zero rather than NULL when empty. The result matches the reference (792800 cents).

The joins connect orders, customers and unit prices without removing eligible product lines. The predicate places the reference date 2026-09-25 on or after a customer's 25th birthday and strictly before their 26th birthday, correctly selecting completed age 25 on that date. The resulting revenue matches the reference (590320 cents).

The query restricts order lines to product IDs a, b and c and dates >= 2026-01-01 00:00:00 and < 2026-07-01 00:00:00. The product join supplies prices, SUM(quantity_product * price) computes revenue excluding VAT in cents, and COALESCE handles an empty selection. It returns the reference value (936350 cents).

The order-date predicate implements the required interval [2026-01-01 00:00:00, 2026-10-01 00:00:00), including the start and excluding the end. All products are retained; each line contributes its quantity multiplied by unit price, and COALESCE guarantees a single numeric result. The value matches the reference (2826250 cents).

The query correctly represents the single-day window 2026-06-01: o.date >= '2026-06-01 00:00:00' and o.date < '2026-06-02 00:00:00'. It sums quantities times product prices across matching order lines rather than simply counting orders or adding unit prices. The computed total equals the reference (38480 cents).

The query searches the half-open period from 2025-01-01 00:00:00 to 2026-01-01 00:00:00. No order lines satisfy the filter in the provided database, and COALESCE(SUM(...), 0) correctly returns 0 rather than NULL, with the required revenue_cents alias. This matches the reference (0 cents).

The conditions select orders from 2026-05-31 00:00:00 inclusive to 2026-06-01 00:00:00 exclusive, avoiding the common mistake of including the following day. The query joins product prices and sums o.quantity_product * p.price for every qualifying line; COALESCE preserves a scalar result. It matches the reference (13970 cents).

The SQL requires birth year 2001 and a birthday already passed. It omits customers born in late 2000 who are still 25 on 2026-09-26. In this dataset, customer C007 (born 2000-11-30) is omitted, losing 118740 cents.

The SQL requires order year minus birth year to equal 25 and the birthday to have occurred. It excludes customers for whom the year difference is 26 but whose 26th birthday is still upcoming; those customers are still 25 when ordering. This omits 59 eligible order lines worth 439570 cents.

The SQL computes completed age 25 on 2026-12-01 using two cases: birth-year difference 25 with the birthday already reached, or difference 26 with the next birthday still ahead. Both cases use month-day comparisons, correctly capturing the full age-25 cohort rather than a single birth year or date. The resulting total matches the reference (446690 cents).

The product filter IN ('a', 'b', 'c') includes exactly the requested product IDs and applies no date restriction, as the question covers all orders. The product join provides each unit price and SUM(o.quantity_product * p.price) measures line revenue in cents excluding VAT, with COALESCE for empty sets. It matches the reference (1666490 cents).

The query selects only products a and c and implements the half-open April 2026 window with o.date >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' and o.date < '2026-05-01 00:00:00'. Aggregating quantities times unit prices across those lines yields the reference amount of 107740 cents; COALESCE guarantees a value if no lines match.

The query correctly combines product IDs a, b and c with the half-open interval [2026-10-01 00:00:00, 2026-12-01 00:00:00). No lines match both conditions in the dataset, so COALESCE returns 0 instead of NULL. The resulting value agrees with the reference (0 cents).

The SQL applies the March-to-June half-open order window and computes age 25 on the separate reference date 2026-09-25, rather than at the order date. Its two birthday cases cover people with a year difference of 25 whose birthday has passed and those with a difference of 26 whose birthday has not yet occurred. The computed revenue matches the reference (168680 cents). Note: the returned SELECT includes an inline SQL comment despite the prompt requesting no comments.
